source.original_text: ASTIS-authored generic library statement, not an attribution of an arbitrary-space theorem to the paper. Two normalized nonnegative densities satisfy both sharp TV–affinity comparisons. 1-a\le\delta=\frac12\int|f-g|\,d\mu\le\sqrt{1-a^2},\qquad0\le a\le1. \((X,\mathcal A,\mu)\) is any measure space. No finiteness, probability or sigma-finiteness assumption is made on the reference measure \(\mu\). \(f,g:X\to\mathbb R\) are measurable, nonnegative at every point, genuinely integrable, and satisfy \(\int f\,d\mu=\int g\,d\mu=1\). These define the generic density contract; the actual paper theorem has none of them as additional caller hypotheses. This is a pointwise representative contract, not a claim of the weakest a.e. interface. Event masses are the actual density set integrals; actual-law consumers must identify them with the matching measures. a=\int\sqrt{fg}\,d\mu,\qquad\delta=\sup_{B\in\mathcal A}\left|\int_Bf\,d\mu-\int_Bg\,d\mu\right|.

∀ {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α]
    (μ : Measure α) {f g : α → ℝ}
    (hf0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x) (hg0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ g x)
    (hfm : Measurable f) (hgm : Measurable g)
    (hfi : Integrable f μ) (hgi : Integrable g μ)
    (hf1 : (∫ x, f x ∂μ) = 1) (hg1 : (∫ x, g x ∂μ) = 1),
    let a : ℝ := ∫ x, Real.sqrt (f x * g x) ∂μ
    let δ : ℝ := sSup {z : ℝ | ∃ B : Set α, MeasurableSet B ∧
      z = |(∫ x in B, f x ∂μ) - (∫ x in B, g x ∂μ)|}
    Integrable (fun x => Real.sqrt (f x * g x)) μ ∧
    0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 ∧
    δ = (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (∫ x, |f x - g x| ∂μ) ∧
    1 - a ≤ δ ∧ δ ≤ Real.sqrt (1 - a ^ 2)
decoder_context: The carrier is an arbitrary measurable space; μ is an arbitrary measure, not assumed finite, probability or sigma-finite. f and g are real functions. Measurable means ordinary measurability; Integrable means genuine Bochner absolute integrability.

All integrals explicitly use μ or its restriction to the displayed event. sSup is the real conditional-complete supremum. Real.sqrt is the nonnegative real square root, with totalized conventions outside its nonnegative domain. The statement asserts actual integrability and range, not a fallback-integral convention.

import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Set

/-!
# Normalized density TV and Hellinger affinity

A shared library interface on an arbitrary common measure space. The inputs
are genuine nonnegative measurable L1 densities of mass one. Event discrepancy
is exactly half the L1 difference and lies between 1-affinity and sqrt(1-a²).
No probability/finiteness assumption is made on the reference measure.
Paper consumers must derive all density conditions from their actual laws.
-/

open MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.InformationTheory.DensityAffinity
set_option autoImplicit false

theorem normalized_density_tv_affinity {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α]
    (μ : Measure α) {f g : α → ℝ}
    (hf0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x) (hg0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ g x)
    (hfm : Measurable f) (hgm : Measurable g)
    (hfi : Integrable f μ) (hgi : Integrable g μ)
    (hf1 : (∫ x, f x ∂μ) = 1) (hg1 : (∫ x, g x ∂μ) = 1) :
    let a : ℝ := ∫ x, Real.sqrt (f x * g x) ∂μ
    let δ : ℝ := sSup {z : ℝ | ∃ B : Set α, MeasurableSet B ∧
      z = |(∫ x in B, f x ∂μ) - (∫ x in B, g x ∂μ)|}
    Integrable (fun x => Real.sqrt (f x * g x)) μ ∧
    0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 ∧
    δ = (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (∫ x, |f x - g x| ∂μ) ∧
    1 - a ≤ δ ∧ δ ≤ Real.sqrt (1 - a ^ 2) := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let F : α → ℝ := fun x => Real.sqrt (f x)
  let G : α → ℝ := fun x => Real.sqrt (g x)
  let a : ℝ := ∫ x, Real.sqrt (f x * g x) ∂μ
  let d : α → ℝ := fun x => f x - g x
  let D : Set ℝ := {z | ∃ B : Set α, MeasurableSet B ∧
    z = |(∫ x in B, f x ∂μ) - (∫ x in B, g x ∂μ)|}
  let H : ℝ := (1 / 2 : ℝ) * ∫ x, |d x| ∂μ
  have hFs (x : α) : F x ^ 2 = f x := Real.sq_sqrt (hf0 x)
  have hGs (x : α) : G x ^ 2 = g x := Real.sq_sqrt (hg0 x)
  have hF0 (x : α) : 0 ≤ F x := Real.sqrt_nonneg _
  have hG0 (x : α) : 0 ≤ G x := Real.sqrt_nonneg _
  have hF : MemLp F 2 μ :=
    (memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq (by dsimp [F]; fun_prop)).2
      (hfi.congr (Filter.Eventually.of_forall (fun x => (hFs x).symm)))
  have hG : MemLp G 2 μ :=
    (memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq (by dsimp [G]; fun_prop)).2
      (hgi.congr (Filter.Eventually.of_forall (fun x => (hGs x).symm)))
  have hmul : Integrable (fun x => F x * G x) μ := hF.integrable_mul hG
  have hprod (x : α) : Real.sqrt (f x * g x) = F x * G x :=
    Real.sqrt_mul (hf0 x) (g x)
  have hL : Integrable (fun x => Real.sqrt (f x * g x)) μ :=
    hmul.congr (Filter.Eventually.of_forall (fun x => (hprod x).symm))
  have ha : (∫ x, F x * G x ∂μ) = a := by
    exact integral_congr_ae (Filter.Eventually.of_forall (fun x => (hprod x).symm))
  have ha0 : 0 ≤ a := integral_nonneg (fun x => Real.sqrt_nonneg _)
  have ha1 : a ≤ 1 := by
    have hc := integral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq_of_nonneg
      (p := 2) (q := 2) (Real.holderConjugate_iff.mpr (by norm_num))
      (Filter.Eventually.of_forall hF0) (Filter.Eventually.of_forall hG0)
      (by simpa using hF) (by simpa using hG)
    simp_rw [Real.rpow_two, hFs, hGs] at hc
    rw [hf1, hg1, ha] at hc
    norm_num at hc
    exact hc
  have hdi : Integrable d μ := hfi.sub hgi
  have hd0 : (∫ x, d x ∂μ) = 0 := by
    dsimp [d]
    rw [integral_sub hfi hgi, hf1, hg1, sub_self]
  have hH0 : 0 ≤ H := mul_nonneg (by norm_num) (integral_nonneg (fun _ => abs_nonneg _))
  -- Equal total masses give the factor-one-half event bound.
  have hevent (B : Set α) (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
      |(∫ x in B, f x ∂μ) - (∫ x in B, g x ∂μ)| ≤ H := by
    rw [← integral_sub hfi.integrableOn hgi.integrableOn]
    change |∫ x in B, d x ∂μ| ≤ H
    have hs := integral_add_compl hB hdi
    rw [hd0] at hs
    have hcompl : (∫ x in Bᶜ, d x ∂μ) = -(∫ x in B, d x ∂μ) := by linarith
    have h1 := abs_integral_le_integral_abs (μ := μ.restrict B) (f := d)
    have h2 := abs_integral_le_integral_abs (μ := μ.restrict Bᶜ) (f := d)
    rw [hcompl, abs_neg] at h2
    have hsabs := integral_add_compl hB hdi.abs
    dsimp only [H]
    linarith
  have hDne : D.Nonempty := ⟨0, ∅, MeasurableSet.empty, by simp⟩
  have hDbd : BddAbove D := by
    refine ⟨H, ?_⟩
    rintro z ⟨B, hB, rfl⟩
    exact hevent B hB
  have hsup_le : sSup D ≤ H := by
    apply csSup_le hDne
    rintro z ⟨B, hB, rfl⟩
    exact hevent B hB
  -- The positive set attains half the L1 norm of the zero-mass difference.
  let B : Set α := {x | 0 ≤ d x}
  have hB : MeasurableSet B := measurableSet_le measurable_const (hfm.sub hgm)
  have hpos : (fun x => (d x)⁺) = B.indicator d := by
    funext x
    by_cases hx : 0 ≤ d x
    · simp [B, Set.indicator_of_mem, hx, PosPart.posPart]
    · simp [B, Set.indicator_of_notMem, hx, PosPart.posPart,
        max_eq_right (le_of_lt (lt_of_not_ge hx))]
  have hattain : H = ∫ x in B, d x ∂μ := by
    have he := integral_abs_eq_two_mul_integral_posPart_sub_integral hdi
    rw [hd0, hpos, integral_indicator hB] at he
    dsimp only [H]
    linarith
  have hsup_ge : H ≤ sSup D := by
    have he := le_csSup hDbd (show |(∫ x in B, f x ∂μ) - (∫ x in B, g x ∂μ)| ∈ D
      from ⟨B, hB, rfl⟩)
    rw [← integral_sub hfi.integrableOn hgi.integrableOn] at he
    change |∫ x in B, d x ∂μ| ≤ sSup D at he
    rw [← hattain, abs_of_nonneg hH0] at he
    exact he
  have htv : sSup D = H := le_antisymm hsup_le hsup_ge
  -- min(f,g) ≤ sqrt(f*g) gives the lower comparison.
  have hpoint (x : α) : f x + g x - 2 * Real.sqrt (f x * g x) ≤ |d x| := by
    dsimp only [d]
    by_cases hx : f x ≤ g x
    · rw [abs_of_nonpos (sub_nonpos.mpr hx)]
      have hh : f x ≤ Real.sqrt (f x * g x) :=
        Real.le_sqrt_of_sq_le (by nlinarith [hf0 x])
      linarith
    · rw [abs_of_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr (le_of_lt (lt_of_not_ge hx)))]
      have hh : g x ≤ Real.sqrt (f x * g x) :=
        Real.le_sqrt_of_sq_le (by nlinarith [hg0 x])
      linarith
  have hlower : 1 - a ≤ sSup D := by
    have hi := integral_mono ((hfi.add hgi).sub (hL.const_mul 2)) hdi.abs hpoint
    change (∫ x, f x + g x - 2 * Real.sqrt (f x * g x) ∂μ) ≤ _ at hi
    rw [integral_sub (f := fun x => f x + g x) (hfi.add hgi) (hL.const_mul 2), integral_add hfi hgi,
      integral_const_mul, hf1, hg1] at hi
    change 1 + 1 - 2 * a ≤ _ at hi
    rw [htv]
    dsimp only [H]
    linarith
  -- Cauchy-Schwarz on |sqrt f - sqrt g| and sqrt f + sqrt g.
  have hminus : MemLp (fun x => |F x - G x|) 2 μ := by
    simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs, Pi.sub_apply] using (hF.sub hG).norm
  have hplus : MemLp (fun x => F x + G x) 2 μ := hF.add hG
  have hminusInt : (∫ x, (F x - G x) ^ 2 ∂μ) = 2 - 2 * a := by
    calc
      _ = ∫ x, (f x + g x) - 2 * (F x * G x) ∂μ := by
        apply integral_congr_ae
        exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => by nlinarith [hFs x, hGs x]
      _ = 2 - 2 * a := by
        rw [integral_sub (f := fun x => f x + g x) (hfi.add hgi) (hmul.const_mul 2), integral_add hfi hgi,
          integral_const_mul, hf1, hg1, ha]
        ring
  have hplusInt : (∫ x, (F x + G x) ^ 2 ∂μ) = 2 + 2 * a := by
    calc
      _ = ∫ x, (f x + g x) + 2 * (F x * G x) ∂μ := by
        apply integral_congr_ae
        exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => by nlinarith [hFs x, hGs x]
      _ = 2 + 2 * a := by
        rw [integral_add (f := fun x => f x + g x) (hfi.add hgi) (hmul.const_mul 2), integral_add hfi hgi,
          integral_const_mul, hf1, hg1, ha]
        ring
  have hc := integral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq_of_nonneg
    (p := 2) (q := 2) (Real.holderConjugate_iff.mpr (by norm_num))
    (Filter.Eventually.of_forall (fun x => abs_nonneg (F x - G x)))
    (Filter.Eventually.of_forall (fun x => add_nonneg (hF0 x) (hG0 x)))
    (by simpa using hminus) (by simpa using hplus)
  simp_rw [Real.rpow_two, sq_abs] at hc
  rw [hminusInt, hplusInt] at hc
  simp only [← Real.sqrt_eq_rpow] at hc
  have hfactor (x : α) : |d x| = |F x - G x| * (F x + G x) := by
    calc
      _ = |(F x - G x) * (F x + G x)| := by
        congr 1
        dsimp only [d]
        nlinarith [hFs x, hGs x]
      _ = _ := by rw [abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (add_nonneg (hF0 x) (hG0 x))]
  have hroot : Real.sqrt (2 - 2 * a) * Real.sqrt (2 + 2 * a) =
      2 * Real.sqrt (1 - a ^ 2) := by
    rw [← Real.sqrt_mul (by linarith : 0 ≤ 2 - 2 * a),
      show (2 - 2 * a) * (2 + 2 * a) = 4 * (1 - a ^ 2) by ring,
      Real.sqrt_mul (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 4)]
    rw [show Real.sqrt (4 : ℝ) = 2 by
      convert Real.sqrt_sq (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2) using 1
      norm_num]
  have hupper : sSup D ≤ Real.sqrt (1 - a ^ 2) := by
    have hi : (∫ x, |d x| ∂μ) ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt (1 - a ^ 2) := by
      simp_rw [hfactor]
      exact hc.trans_eq hroot
    rw [htv]
    dsimp only [H]
    linarith
  exact ⟨hL, ha0, ha1, htv, hlower, hupper⟩

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.InformationTheory.DensityAffinity

notation.text: Affinity uses a real Bochner integral; its true L1 and range are conclusions. The event supremum is over measurable sets only.

steps.title: Place square-root densities in L2
steps.text: The squared square roots are the original nonnegative densities. Their squared integrals are one. Cauchy–Schwarz gives both genuine integrability of their product and affinity at most one; its nonnegative integrand gives the other endpoint.
steps.formula: F=\sqrt f,\ G=\sqrt g,\quad\int F^2=\int G^2=1,\quad FG=\sqrt{fg}\in L^1,\quad0\le a\le1.
steps.lean: hF/hG use memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq. hmul uses MemLp.integrable_mul; hprod uses Real.sqrt_mul; ha1 uses integral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq_of_nonneg.

steps.title: Obtain the sharp half factor on every event
steps.text: Let d=f−g. It has total integral zero, so an event integral and its complement have opposite values. Bound the absolute integral on each part by the corresponding integral of |d| and add. The event-value set is nonempty and bounded.
steps.lean: hd0 follows from the unit masses; hevent uses integral_add_compl and abs_integral_le_integral_abs. hDne/hDbd and csSup_le produce the upper bound for the supremum.

steps.title: Attain the bound on the positive set
steps.text: The measurable set where d≥0 attains the positive-part integral. Since the total integral vanishes, the positive part is half the L1 norm. This proves equality with normalized event TV.
steps.lean: hpos identifies the positive part with B.indicator d. hattain uses integral_abs_eq_two_mul_integral_posPart_sub_integral and integral_indicator. le_csSup and hsup_le give htv.

steps.title: Derive the lower affinity comparison
steps.text: For nonnegative values, the smaller of f and g is at most their geometric mean. Equivalently, f+g−2√(fg)≤|f−g|. Integrate this inequality and use both masses and the exact TV identity.
steps.lean: hpoint uses Real.le_sqrt_of_sq_le in the two value orderings; hlower applies integral_mono with actual L1 of every term.

steps.title: Derive the upper affinity comparison
steps.text: Factor the density difference through the sum and difference of square roots. Their squares integrate to 2±2a. Cauchy–Schwarz, followed by nonnegative square-root algebra, gives the upper bound.
steps.lean: hminus/hplus establish L2; hminusInt/hplusInt expand the integrals. hc is the same canonical Mathlib Cauchy–Schwarz node, hfactor and hroot give the exact algebra, and hupper concludes.

reconstruction.text:
Let α be any type equipped with a measurable-space structure. For every measure μ on α and every pair of real-valued functions f,g : α → ℝ, assume, in this order, that f(x) ≥ 0 for every x ∈ α, that g(x) ≥ 0 for every x ∈ α, that f is measurable, that g is measurable, that f is integrable with respect to μ, that g is integrable with respect to μ, that ∫_α f(x) dμ(x) = 1, and that ∫_α g(x) dμ(x) = 1. The measure μ is arbitrary: no finiteness, probability, or sigma-finiteness assumption is imposed.

Define the real numbers
  a = ∫_α √(f(x)g(x)) dμ(x),
  δ = sup {z ∈ ℝ : there exists a measurable set B ⊆ α such that z = |∫_B f(x) dμ(x) − ∫_B g(x) dμ(x)|}.
Here each integral over B is taken with respect to the restriction of μ to B, the supremum is the real conditionally complete supremum, and √ is the nonnegative real square root with its totalized real convention.

Then x ↦ √(f(x)g(x)) is integrable with respect to μ, and all of the following hold:
  0 ≤ a,
  a ≤ 1,
  δ = (1/2) ∫_α |f(x) − g(x)| dμ(x),
  1 − a ≤ δ,
  δ ≤ √(1 − a²).
All displayed integrals of real-valued functions are real Bochner integrals, and integrability means absolute Bochner integrability. The exponent 2 in a² is the natural-number exponent 2.
